facts.rationale: Separates directly visible indexing formulas and callback assignments from unproven numeric bounds and compiled adjacency.
facts.value: Pickup selects state 0. Release clamps stored charge against the stored maximum and selects charge + 1; terrain impact applies the same clamp and selects charge + 10. The declared table assigns Motion8 callbacks to entries 1–8, Motion9 to entry 9, and Motion17 to entries 10–17. These declared ranges do not themselves prove the externally supplied maximum charge or validate every calculated index. The separately declared three-entry sound array is indexed by HSD_Randi(3) during active oscillation updates and passed to Item_8026AF0C.

evidence.why: Distinct travel and impact suites, including enabled-hitbox scale restoration.

facts.rationale: Preserves supported lifecycle mapping while removing unsupported harmlessness and retaining the distinct state-9 branch.
facts.value: Organizes the native Mewtwo and copied-Mewtwo Kirby Shadow Ball article into attached charging presentation, charge-indexed Motion8 travel, a distinct Motion9 traveling variant, and charge-indexed Motion17 terrain-impact aftermath. Travel includes an oscillating child-model offset. Impact hides the model and spawns an effect, but its animation callback also restores an enabled hitbox's stored impact scale; these callbacks do not establish that the aftermath is non-damaging.

evidence.why: Guarded impact entry and hitbox-scale consumer.

facts.rationale: Corrects the claim that the no-contact path leaves all item state unchanged and identifies the actual consumer of x64.
facts.value: Each invocation calls the directional collision helper, including its unconditional collision refresh. If no qualifying contact is reported, this callback performs no impact transition and returns false. On qualifying contact it invokes the common impact helper, which hides the model, resets lifetime, replaces effects, clears x28, clamps charge against the stored maximum, selects charge + 10, clears on_accessory, stores hitbox-zero scale times attr->x24 in x64, and emits effect and sound. Motion17 animation later copies x64 back to hitbox-zero scale when that hitbox is enabled. The collision callback returns false in either case.

facts.rationale: Corrects the half-interval sign-reversal claim and preserves the exceptional initial counter state.
facts.value: When x4C is not positive, clears the child-model displacement; otherwise increments x48 and, when x48 >= attr->x20, resets x48, perturbs the oscillation angle, sets x44 = -x40 / (0.5 * attr->x20), and selects a random sound. Every active tick then adds x44 to x40 and accumulates projected displacement. The helper always writes model translation and increments x4C. The held constructor initializes x48 to attr->x20, so the first active update reaches the threshold for ordinary positive intervals. With a fixed positive interval T and ideal arithmetic, the new delta takes amplitude A to zero after T/2 updates and to -A after T updates; discrete threshold timing and floating-point rounding qualify this description.

facts.rationale: Replaces the incorrect orientation interpretation with the model-scale value returned by the canonical callee and consumed by held transforms.
facts.value: If common item creation returns null, returns null without item-specific initialization. On success, clears the four item-command variables, installs attribute-defined lifetime, initializes held-state markers, vectors and oscillation seeds, records the originating fighter in x2C, stores that fighter's model scale in x54, and attaches the article to the supplied bone. The later held animation callback conditionally queries the matching retained owner for charge and uses x54 to scale the inverse cached model translation.

facts.rationale: Corrects the intermediate-state label using direct constructor behavior and the documented forward-throw caller.
facts.value: Shadow Ball article module declaring an eighteen-entry ItemStateTable: attached state 0, eight Motion8 travel entries 1–8, distinct Motion9 traveling entry 9, and eight Motion17 impact entries 10–17, plus a three-entry s32 sound-ID array. A separate constructor directly initializes state 9 for forward-throw shots; it is not an intermediate state required between normal release and impact.

evidence.why: Release indexing, travel suites and impact behavior.

facts.rationale: Preserves lifecycle behavior while replacing the misleading intermediate phase and making numeric-state uncertainty explicit.
facts.value: State 0 handles the attached article. Normal release selects stored charge + 1, while the separate forward-throw constructor directly selects state 9. Motion8 travel maintains scale, lifetime, guarded polar velocity and oscillating model offset; Motion9 retains lifetime and terrain collision but has empty local physics. Both travel collision suites can enter stored charge + 10. The Motion17 impact suite restores stored model and enabled-hitbox scales, resets velocity and returns false from collision. Declared callback ranges do not establish the externally supplied maximum charge or guarantee every calculated index.
